newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-GANGULY HITS TEST BEST 147.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-GANGULY HITS TEST BEST 147.

text.p: Saurav Ganguly hit his highest test score of 147 as India took a slender first innings lead of 43 on the third day of the final test against Sri Lanka on Monday.
By the close, Sri Lanka had reached 77 for the loss of Marvan Attapattu who edged an awkward climbing delivery from leg-spinner Anil Kumble to Mohammed Azharuddin at slip shortly before the close.
Sanath Jayasuriya, who made 340 in the first test, was undefeated on 34.
Ganguly resumed his innings on 47 in the morning and extended a fine stand with captain Sachin Tendulkar to 150, a record for India's fifth wicket against Sri Lanka, before Tendulkar fell for 139.

The Indian captain, who was dropped on 34, had posted his 13th test century on Sunday and was finally dismissed when a flowing cover drive off Ravindra Pushpakumara was brilliantly caught by Muthiah Muralitharan at extra cover. He batted for 403 minutes and faced 266 balls, hitting 16 fours.

Ganguly then held the innings together as left-arm fast-medium bowler Sajeeva de Silva and off-spinner Muralitharan worked their way through the rest of the batting. Muralitharan took three for eight in 19 balls to finish with four for 99.
Only wicketkeeper Nayan Mongia, who contributed 15 in 108 minutes to a sixth wicket partnership of 52, gave him any worthwhile support.
When Ganguly was finally out, caught by Chaminda Vaas off Sajeeva de Silva, he had faced 309 balls in 426 minutes and hit 19 fours.
